_: The mother. Drawn for jt-golden-goose. The channel's second human character; read
cast/gardener/cast.json first -- everything it says about drawing a person rather than
a type applies here and applies harder, because she is the one who does the wrong thing.
SHE IS NOT A VILLAIN AND MUST NEVER BE DRAWN AS ONE. The story is explicit that she is a
widow keeping four people fed, and that the thought crept up on her over weeks. Drawn
tired and drawn kind; the reaching cell is a woman reaching, not a woman snatching.
docs/01: never make the video braver than the text.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT: any caste or religious marker, bindi or sindoor -- a widow's
presentation is a live and painful subject in Indian households and this channel does
not make a costume of it. Plain clothes, no jewellery. A HUMAN SHOULD LOOK AT THIS SHEET.

cells.mother-sew: An ordinary Indian woman in her late thirties, FULL BODY, sitting cross-legged on the floor in three-quarter view facing LEFT, bent over a piece of cloth in her lap with a needle in one raised hand, sewing. Warm brown skin, black hair pulled back in a low plain bun, a plain undyed cotton sari worn simply, no border pattern. A calm tired face, eyes down at the work, mouth closed. NO caste or religious mark of any kind, NO bindi, NO sindoor, NO heavy jewellery, NO exaggerated features, NO comic exaggeration. Bare feet. IN THE SAME HAND AS THE REFERENCE ANIMALS: thick soft warm-brown outlines of the SAME WEIGHT as the goose's, FLAT CEL SHADING ONLY -- no gradients, no airbrushing, no gloss, no shine on the skin. Simplified picture-book cartoon proportions, a slightly large head, simple hands, soft rounded shapes. Children's picture-book cartoon, NOT a stock vector illustration.
